Question Choices: For independent events complete the multiplication rule P(A and B)=____.
Hints: Independence means no effect on each other.;Multiply the two probabilities.
Solution: Independence means the joint probability factors: P(A and B)=P(A)*P(B). This equation is the general test for independence, including zero-probability cases. When P(A)>0 it is equivalent to P(B given A)=P(B).

Question Choices: A student guesses uniformly at random on two independent true-false questions. Find the probability both are wrong.
Hints: Each guess is wrong with probability 1/2.;Multiply.
Solution: Each uniform true-false guess has probability 1/2 of the requested result. Independent guesses give (1/2)(1/2)=1/4=0.25 for both requested results.

Question Choices: A bag has 2 red and 3 blue balls. Draw uniformly at random without replacement. Find P(blue then blue).
Hints: The first draw has probability 3/5.;The second has probability 2/4.
Solution: The first blue probability is 3/5. Given a blue first draw, 2 blue balls remain among 4, so the second conditional probability is 2/4. Multiply: (3/5)*(2/4)=3/10. Both numerator and denominator change.

Question Choices: For events with P(A)>0, complete the general multiplication rule P(A and B)=P(A)____.
Hints: Use a conditional probability.;The second factor assumes A happened.
Solution: Conditional probability satisfies P(B given A)=P(A and B)/P(A), with P(A)>0. Multiply by P(A) to get P(A and B)=P(A)P(B given A). This rule applies whether or not the events are independent.

Question Choices: A fair six-sided die numbered 1 through 6 is rolled independently twice. Find the probability of a 6 then a 6.
Solution: Each roll gives a 6 with probability 1/6. Independence permits multiplication: (1/6)(1/6)=1/36.
